title: It Don't Mean a Thing and the title's origin
summary: Cootie says he used to tell Duke 'it don't mean a thing if it ain't got that swing', which became the 1932 title.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Let's talk about in 1932, one of the big sessions was "Don't Mean a Thing". Now what's your memory on that? Who was involved in there? Can you remember? "If it
ain't got that swing." I mean, where did that come -- who did that come out of, or how did that come about? Do you think.
It came out of me.
No. Really? Did it?
Yeah. The saying. The saying I used to tell him. I used to tell Duke, I said, "Man, it don't mean a thing if it ain't got that swing."
(Laughter)
Because if it ain't got the swing, it ain't got no beat. It's got to swing.
Yeah.
Yeah. So that's how the title came about.
Yeah.
It don't mean a thing if it ain't got that swing.
Well, listen. That had to be born with words and music. That didn't get born in just music. I mean that had to come because of doo-wah, doo-wah, and all that. It came right out of it, didn't it?
Yeah. Uh-huh.
So maybe you're -- your saying that to Duke, he just simply --
He got something out of it.
He got something out of it. He -- it
just came right out on the piano. I guess that's just what happened, isn't it?

And he probably said to you, 'Doo-wah,' and you did this. You picked it up from there. After all, that's surely one of the biggest numbers he ever had. I mean, to this day, when his name's mentioned, that comes up. And it's used by other people for all kinds -- I mean, it's used by writers and it's just a truism. It's a tradition, by now. 'It Don't Mean a Thing if it Ain't Got that Swing.' So you contributed something to the English language, Cootie, with that one.
(Laughter)
Because that just applied to everything. Yeah. I guess the guys were -- I guess everybody was kind of thrilled with that, weren't they, when you made that number?
I don't think so.
No?
No.
